newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain cites progress in China-HK troop talks.
newsitem.headline: Britain cites progress in China-HK troop talks.

text.p: Britain reported progress on Thursday in talks with China on Beijing's plan to send troops to Hong Kong ahead of the British colony's return to Chinese rule.

Alan Paul, British representative in the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group hammering out details of China's takeover of the territory this July 1, told Hong Kong radio that Beijing agreed to supply information sought by Britain.
Speaking after a meeting of the diplomatic group, he said the two sides had yet to reach a final agreement.
Before the meeting, Paul told reporters Britain had asked China for data on the advance military units, including their size and functions.
"We need details to explain the functions of the personnel, the numbers. We need to know about such technical things as the radio frequencies that they will be using," Paul told reporters.
"We still need further information from the Chinese side. detailed information about their plan, then we can evaluate that," he said. And China had agreed to cooperate.

"Our objective is to reach agreement with the Chinese side on a reasonable number of advance personnel, arrival at a suitable time and liaising with the British side, that's the garrison in the Hong Kong government, in an appropriate way," he said.
Britain is scaling down its garrison in Hong Kong, and all its troops will have gone from the territory by July 1.
The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) will then take over defence responsibilities in Hong Kong.
Under the 1984 handover treaty, the territory will become an autonomous capitalist region of communist-ruled China, running all its own affairs except defence and diplomacy.
